articles.excerpt: My agent handed me a draft that opened with a scene from my own life: On October 19, I wrote down one rule for every overnight OpenClaw job I run: "work on this overnight" is a request, not a schedule…
articles.body: My agent handed me a draft that opened with a scene from my own life: On October 19, I wrote down one rule for every overnight OpenClaw job I run: "work on this overnight" is a request, not a scheduler. I never wrote that sentence. There was no October 19 writing session, no notebook, no rule I sat down and recorded. The agent invented it, because my voice guide told it to open on a concrete, countable instance of my own work. The draft passed the guide. That's a bug in the file, but it isn't the interesting one. The interesting one is that I had no way to know whether the file was doing anything at all — and I'd been running it for a month. The month of credit Twenty-odd rules. A paragraph cap. A seven-question sign-off at the end of every draft.

articles.title: Supabase's October 30 change: what it fixes for your app's security, and what it doesn't
articles.excerpt: On 30 October 2026, Supabase changes how new tables are exposed in existing projects. It's a good security change, but it's easy to misread as "my database is now safe". It isn't: tables you already h…
articles.body: On 30 October 2026 , Supabase changes how new tables are exposed in existing projects. It's a good security change, but it's easy to misread as "my database is now safe". It isn't: tables you already have keep exactly the access they have today. What's changing Until now, every table created in the public schema was automatically granted to the anon , authenticated and service_role roles, so the Data API (REST and GraphQL, which supabase-js uses) could read and write it straight away. Row Level Security was the only thing standing in the way. From 30 October, new tables in public won't get those grants automatically. You have to opt each one in with a Postgres GRANT before your app can reach it through the Data API.

articles.excerpt: IPTV (Internet Protocol Television) has changed how video content is delivered to viewers worldwide. Instead of relying on traditional cable or satellite infrastructure, IPTV uses internet protocols t…
articles.body: IPTV (Internet Protocol Television) has changed how video content is delivered to viewers worldwide. Instead of relying on traditional cable or satellite infrastructure, IPTV uses internet protocols to transmit live television, movies, and on-demand content to compatible devices. But what actually happens behind the scenes when someone opens an IPTV application and starts watching a channel? In this article, we'll explore IPTV architecture, streaming protocols, playlist formats, performance optimization, and the technologies powering modern IPTV platforms. 1. What Is IPTV? IPTV stands for Internet Protocol Television. It is a technology that delivers television content using IP networks rather than traditional broadcasting methods.

articles.excerpt: Why treat builds as code: eliminate drift and make builds a pure function CI integration patterns for hermetic builds and remote cache clients Designing and implementing a Build Doctor diagnostics too…
articles.body: Why treat builds as code: eliminate drift and make builds a pure function CI integration patterns for hermetic builds and remote cache clients Designing and implementing a Build Doctor diagnostics tool Rolling out at scale: onboarding, guardrails, and measuring impact Practical checklists and runbooks for immediate action Treat every build flag, toolchain pin, and cache policy as versioned code — not a local habit. Doing so converts the build from a mutable ritual into a repeatable, auditable function whose outputs are pure and sharable. The pain is specific: slow pull requests because CI redoes work, “works on my machine” debugging, cache-poisoning incidents that invalidate hours of developer effort, and onboarding that takes days because local setups differ.

Later this year, Astrolab will launch its uncrewed moon rover FLIP to the lunar south pole as part of the Griffin Mission 1, or Griffin-1. The California company is one of two that NASA has selected to develop a drivable rover for the agency's Artemis program. On board FLIP will be Hewlett Packard Enterprise's (HPE) Spaceborne Computer-4, an advanced computer module built to be used in space. This will be the first time that high-performance computing and artificial intelligence will be tested on the lunar surface.

articles.title: AI adoption by industry shows what other sectors can learn
articles.excerpt: The current narrative around artificial intelligence in the workplace is largely driven by Silicon Valley. But treating the tech sector as an island misses the actual trends in technology adoption–tec…
articles.body: The current narrative around artificial intelligence in the workplace is largely driven by Silicon Valley. But treating the tech sector as an island misses the actual trends in technology adoption–tech is just the first industry in line. As generative AI and automation tools mature, the shifts currently reshaping software engineering and product management will inevitably filter into healthcare, education, retail, and manufacturing. The variation in adoption rates today isn’t a sign that non-tech industries are falling behind, but rather a reflection of the different speeds at which industries absorb new workflows. For leaders and their teams outside of tech, this differential pace provides a practical blueprint for how AI adoption unfolds, and where the opportunities lie.
